title: Typed Retry Attempt Contract
description: Machine-checkable form of one logged retry attempt in a mission's retry ledger — Goal #5 / docs/ULTIMATE_FRAMEWORK_PLAN.md §C4 ('retry ledger in the mission record: missions/<id>/retries/<task>.attempt-N.md — front-matter: failure state, cause class, what-the-brief-changed; enforced: attempt N+1's brief must differ from attempt N's when cause != transient — a literal diff check'). `failure_state` is conductor/subagent-failure-protocol.md's five-state table verbatim; `cause_class` is its four-class cause-classification table verbatim. This schema validates the SHAPE of one attempt file; the cross-attempt rules (the 3-attempt cap, the same-brief-forbidden-for-non-transient-causes rule) are NOT expressible against a single instance in isolation — they are enforced by `tessctl retry check`/`retry log`, which read the sibling attempt files in `missions/<id>/retries/` before deciding whether a new attempt may even be written (see `_retry_precheck` in `.tess/bin/tessctl`'s MISSION LEDGER region). Flat at the top level (no `retry` wrapper key) — same rationale as mission.schema.json: the primary authored form is a `.md` file with YAML front-matter, where flat keys read most naturally.

mission_id.description: Ties to the mission-states.md FSM record this attempt belongs to (same field name/meaning as crew-plan.schema.json and return-manifest.schema.json's own `mission_id`).

task.description: The task id this retry attempt belongs to — matches a crew-plan Task.id / return-manifest.task_id.

attempt.description: subagent-failure-protocol.md 'Attempt Cap — 3': 'Maximum 3 total attempts on the same task.' A hand-authored attempt-4 file is schema-invalid on its face, belt-and-suspenders alongside `tessctl retry log`'s own refusal to ever write one.

failure_state.description: subagent-failure-protocol.md 'Failure States' table, verbatim (its five rows: Empty return, Partial return, Degraded output, Timeout, Error).

cause_class.description: subagent-failure-protocol.md 'Cause Classification' table, verbatim. Retry rule per class: transient permits a same-brief retry; the other three forbid one ('Same-brief retries are forbidden for every non-transient cause') — enforced by `tessctl retry check`/`retry log`, not by this schema node.

brief_digest_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the whitespace-normalized dispatch brief. The retry ledger stores this commitment, never dispatch-brief plaintext, so the same-brief rule remains deterministic without persisting potentially confidential operator instructions.

brief_length.description: UTF-8 byte length of the whitespace-normalized dispatch brief, stored beside the digest as a transparent format/integrity guard.

brief_change_code.description: Controlled, value-free explanation of the retry relation. Free-text notes are deliberately not persisted in retry records.

logged_at.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp of `tessctl retry log`.

logged_by.description: Who ran `tessctl retry log` (defaults to the OS user).

$comment: Minimal-validator keyword subset supported by tessctl validate: type, enum, const, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, minItems, maxItems, minLength, maxLength, pattern, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, if/then/else, oneOf, anyOf, allOf, contains, $ref, $defs.
